lesson.title: Nativity, Theophany, and Meeting of the Lord

readings.title: Nativity of Christ
readings.text: Thy Nativity, O Christ our God, hath arisen upon the world as the light of wisdom. For at it, they who worshipped the stars were, by a Star, taught to adore thee, the Sun of Righteousness, and to know thee, the Orient from on high. O Lord, glory to thee.

readings.title: Theophany
readings.text: When in Jordan thou wast baptized, O Lord, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest. For the voice of the Father bare witness unto thee, calling thee his beloved Son, and the Spirit, in the form of a Dove, confirmed the steadfastness of that word: O Christ our God, who didst manifest thyself, and dost enlighten the world, glory to thee.

readings.title: Meeting of the Lord
readings.locator: Meeting of the Lord, p.198; troparion
readings.text: Hail, O Virgin Birth-giver of God: for from thee hath shone forth the Sun of Righteousness, Christ our God, who giveth light to those who are in darkness. And rejoice, thou aged, righteous man, that didst receive in thine arms the Redeemer of our souls, who giveth unto us resurrection.

scripture.translation: KJV (public domain in the United States)
scripture.text: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

overview.text: Nativity, Theophany and the Meeting of the Lord concern Christ’s birth and manifestation in human life. The hymn texts express those events in the language of the Incarnation, while the linked articles identify their biblical and liturgical setting.

readings.title: What does the Nativity hymn teach?

paragraphs.text: Nativity means birth; this hymn concerns the birth of Jesus Christ. It describes the star leading those who had worshipped the stars toward recognition of Christ. Its images of light and the Sun of Righteousness present his birth as the revelation of divine wisdom.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: What does the Theophany hymn reveal about the Trinity?

paragraphs.text: Theophany means the manifestation of God. The hymn associates Christ’s baptism in the Jordan with the Father’s testimony and the Spirit’s appearance as a dove. Its central teaching is the manifestation of the Trinity at that event.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: Who is the elder receiving Christ?

paragraphs.text: The righteous elder in the hymn is Simeon, identified in the Gospel account summarized by the linked OCA article on the Meeting. The hymn addresses Mary as Mother of God and Christ as the Redeemer who grants resurrection. It connects the child received in human arms with the saving identity confessed of him.

readings.title: The Nativity in an OCA explanation

paragraphs.text: The OCA article explains the Nativity as the birth in human life of the eternal Son of God. It describes the feast’s services and their scriptural themes.

readings.title: Why is Theophany also called Epiphany?

paragraphs.text: The OCA article explains Epiphany as manifestation and Theophany as the manifestation of God. Its account places Christ’s baptism and the revelation of Father, Son and Holy Spirit at the centre of the feast.

paragraphs.text: The OCA article identifies the event as Christ’s presentation in the Jerusalem Temple and his meeting with Simeon and the prophetess Anna. Their recognition of the child as the promised Christ gives the feast its biblical setting in Luke 2.
